title: Consecration gives each family a secured portion by need
setting: This revelation came at Thompson, Ohio, on 20 May 1831. About sixty members from Colesville, New York, had just arrived under Newel Knight’s lead. They settled on land Leman Copley offered at Thompson. Bishop Edward Partridge was responsible for settling them under the law of consecration. He asked for direction, and Joseph Smith inquired of the Lord. Copley soon withdrew his offer, so the plan was not carried out there.
summary: The revelation gives Edward Partridge directions for organizing the newly arrived people. He and his chosen helpers are to assign each family a portion by its needs. Each person receives a written deed that secures his portion. If a person transgresses and is judged unworthy to belong, he keeps only the deeded portion, not what he consecrated. An agent is to use the remaining money for food and clothing. The bishop is to keep a storehouse for whatever exceeds the people’s needs. The land is consecrated to them “for a little season”. Faithful, just, and wise stewards are promised eternal life.

contextNote.title: Equal does not mean identical
contextNote.text: The Colesville members arrived needing land and support all at once. Verse 3 tells the bishop how to divide what they had. Each family is to be “equal,” but according to its “circumstances,” “wants,” and needs. Verse 4 then secures each portion with a written deed. Verse 9 explains the goal: that the people “may be one”. In this passage, equality means fair provision for each household’s needs, not the same share for all.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 51–57, “A Faithful, a Just, and a Wise Steward,” takes its title from verse 19. What does verse 9 ask of each person, and how might you practice it with what you manage?
reviewNote: Read all 20 verses. Official heading gives Thompson, Ohio, May 1831, for Bishop Partridge on settling arriving Saints. JSP gives 20 May 1831, the Colesville group of sixty or more, Copley’s offer and its withdrawal before 6 June, and a question about Copley’s title to the land. Kirtland included because the migrants gathered to the Kirtland area first. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary said “leaves the Church”; verse 5 speaks of a person who transgresses and is not accounted worthy to belong, so wording now follows the text.
